decision.reason: evidence sufficient (proxy gate verdict; the open aspects need proposals): On its own, [ev-b25449d452b2] says only that documentation was "corrected" for `rootCertExpiryTimestamp` and `citadel_server_cert_chain_expiry_timestamp`, not what the correction was. The same telemetry section fills that gap. [ev-c3da9e3c81f1] says the docs for the cert-expiry timestamp metrics `rootCertExpiryTimestamp` and `certChainExpiryTimestamp` were updated: they never actually recorded a negative number for expired certificates, so the runtime behaviour did not change. Anyone who relied on the old documented negative values should check the sign of `rootCertExpirySeconds` / `certChainExpirySeconds` instead. That is enough to write the open aspects: the subject is the CA cert-expiry timestamp metrics, the change is a documentation-only correction, and applicability is limited to anyone relying on the old documented behaviour, with no operational change ([ev-40e9ce81a63d] separately covers when these metrics refresh). Confidence is low because I'm inferring the link to [ev-c3da9e3c81f1] from the shared section and topic, and the metric names don't match exactly (`citadel_server_cert_chain_expiry_timestamp` vs `certChainExpiryTimestamp`).
